subject.title: Support multiple gateway tokens for multi-user session isolation

question: Should OpenClaw add a native token-mode principal model for per-user Control UI/webchat identity, and should that model be separate from the broader scoped-token/dispatch-lane design in #92367?
rationale: This changes gateway authentication, public configuration, session identity, and security semantics, so the exact principal and threat model must be chosen by maintainers before implementation.

options.title: Design native per-user token principals now
options.body: Create a first-class gateway token-principal design for shared Control UI/webchat users while coordinating scope vocabulary with #92367.

options.title: Fold this into scoped-token design
options.body: Treat per-user identity as one use case of the #92367 scoped-token and dispatch-lane primitive, reducing duplicate auth models at the cost of a broader design pass.

options.title: Keep this outside core for now
options.body: Continue steering multi-user isolation to trusted-proxy/front-layer identity or separate gateways until maintainers want OpenClaw core to own this boundary.

recommendation.title: Design native per-user token principals now
recommendation.body: Create a first-class gateway token-principal design for shared Control UI/webchat users while coordinating scope vocabulary with #92367.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available routing owner from the gateway auth/security history and docs provenance, and the decision spans security policy plus public docs/config behavior.
